🚀 Startup India, DPIIT reaches Katihar, Bihar

On 3 September 2026, the TEJAS (Transforming Entrepreneurial Journeys Across States and Districts) Workshop was conducted in Katihar, Bihar, bringing together district administration, students, aspiring entrepreneurs and ecosystem stakeholders to promote entrepreneurship and innovation at the grassroots level.

The programme was attended by Shri Ashutosh Dwivedi, District Magistrate, Katihar, who interacted with participants and highlighted the importance of creating a supportive environment for young entrepreneurs to transform local ideas and opportunities into sustainable ventures.

Representing Startup India, DPIIT, Mr. Snehansh Sinha conducted a session on the Startup India ecosystem, covering key government initiatives, schemes, regulatory benefits and support available to startups. The interaction also focused on helping aspiring entrepreneurs better understand the resources available to them as they move from ideation to building and scaling their ventures.

The workshop provided a valuable platform for engaging with young participants and discussing how entrepreneurship can help unlock district-level opportunities, local innovation and employment generation.

✨ Key Highlights:
🚀 Awareness on Startup India initiatives and support mechanisms
🏛️ Interaction with the District Administration on strengthening the local startup ecosystem
💡 Encouraging students and aspiring entrepreneurs to pursue innovative ideas
🤝 Connecting government, institutions and emerging entrepreneurs
🌱 Promoting entrepreneurship as a driver of local economic growth and employment

Through initiatives such as TEJAS, Startup India continues to take the entrepreneurial ecosystem deeper into districts and enable aspiring founders across the country to access opportunities, knowledge and government support.

TANUH, the AI Centre of Excellence in Healthcare hosted at Indian Institute of Science (IISc) and C-CAMP are launching the 'TANUH - C-CAMP Innovations Program,’ focused on identifying and nurturing promising Indian-developed AI-based innovations addressing priority non-communicable disease (NCD) areas.

Indian healthcare is seeing a rapidly escalating NCD burden, with onset of disease being noted as early as the mid-forties, a decade earlier than in most developed nations. 

AI innovations have the potential to revolutionize and democratize this sector in Indian healthcare, with never-before-seen opportunities in diagnostics, screening, prevention, monitoring, therapeutics, and scale-up technologies.

India already has a nascent ecosystem for this that is quietly taking shape. 

To build on this emerging ecosystem, the ‘TANUH - C-CAMP Innovations Program’ is attempting to provide a customised, stage-appropriate support mechanism to selected innovations across three technical readiness level stages:

-Idea to Proof of Concept
- Proof of Concept to Minimum Viable Product
- Deployment ready

NCD focus areas (not limited to):
- Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Diseases
- Cancer (Oral, Breast, Cervical and Lung)
- Chronic Respiratory Disorders
- Musculoskeletal Disorders
- Metabolic Liver Diseases

TANUH's total grant pool of ₹2.25 Cr+ aims to support at least eight startups, offering different types of support based on each startup's stage.

Applications are now open. 
Find all details and the application link: https://lnkd.in/gYzN9qjX 
Deadline: 28th Sept, 2026

What if waste plants could make better decisions with real-time data?

GREEN AADHAAR, a startup part of the Circular Bharat Accelerator, is building the digital infrastructure layer for waste processing facilities. Its platform brings real-time process intelligence to help operators understand plant performance, identify inefficiencies, and optimise operations.

Work in Progress, our monthly newsletter, now reaches close to 30,000 subscribers by email. More than 12,000 people subscribe to it here on LinkedIn, and that number is still climbing.

We chose the name in 2021, and it was not a marketing decision. It was an admission. We did not know how to build markets for innovations that had no business case yet. Five years on, we still do not know entirely. So we publish what we are learning: how our portfolio companies are building and de-risking, how end users and communities are adopting these solutions, and how the ecosystem is evolving.

The appetite for substance is far larger than that, and we have been underestimating our own audience for years. Some subscribers send us feedback. Some write back with corrections, which is the highest form of readership.

Our writing travels only as far as our readers carry it, and the people who most need to read about social impact, entrepreneurship, deep science and patient capital are usually outside our own echo chamber. Please subscribe, read and repost. That means a lot to us.

Social Alpha is still a work in progress. That remains the point.

Delighted to share the successful completion of the "City Camp – Essentials of Scientific Entrepreneurship," a two-day workshop organised by Venture Center and Tamil Nadu Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (TANUVAS) with CSR support from Kemin Industries.

The workshop brought together 130+ participants, including students, startups, aspiring entrepreneurs and innovators, for two days of learning, interaction and hands-on activities focused on taking scientific ideas towards entrepreneurship.

The workshop also featured hands-on exercises, founder interactions, investor perspectives, mentoring clinics and networking opportunities, giving participants a practical understanding of the entrepreneurial journey.

A big thank you to all the participants, speakers, mentors, founders, organisers and partners who made the City Camp a success!

Can cities become the farms of the future?

In this article, Dr. Arpit Shukla, Incubation Manager, VentureStudio Bio-NEST, explores the promise and limitations of urban farming.

From rooftops, basements, and warehouses to hydroponics, aeroponics, and controlled environment agriculture, urban farming is often presented as the future of food. But is it truly a scalable solution, or sometimes just a sustainability theatre?

Dr. Shukla offers a grounded perspective on where urban farming works, where it falls short, and why its real value may lie in climate-conscious, resource-efficient, and resilient city-building.

We are delighted to share that Sense Original, an iCreate-supported startup, has partnered with PW (PhysicsWallah) to tackle counterfeit books.

By integrating SenseOriginal’s authentication tags into Physics Wallah study materials, buyers can easily verify genuine copies. This collaboration marks a key milestone for the startup in scaling its anti-counterfeiting solution across high-volume products.

Congratulations to Mohammed Saalim, Director, Dr. Ashkara Sami, Co-founder & COO, and the entire SenseOriginal team on this achievement!
